claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're asking about, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 16 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm assessing your eligibility for Child Benefit for your son Alex, who is 16 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 16, there are some additional requirements to check. Let me ask you:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school or college anymore. But he has started an apprenticeship in Belfast.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify one important detail:

**What type of apprenticeship has Alex started?** Specifically, is this an apprenticeship in England, or is it an apprenticeship program in Northern Ireland (since you mentioned Belfast)?

This is important because the rules differ depending on the type and location of the apprenticeship.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's an apprenticeship in Northern Ireland - he's doing it in Belfast.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex is doing an apprenticeship in Northern Ireland.

Before I make my final assessment, I need to confirm a few more details about your circumstances:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you the person responsible for Alex - meaning you live with him and/or pay for his upkeep (such as food, clothes, pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with me and I'm responsible for him - I pay for everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me just confirm one final detail:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

You meet the general eligibility criteria - you live in the UK, Alex lives with you, you're responsible for him, and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him. 

However, Alex has started an apprenticeship in Northern Ireland. The rules I have access to specifically state that Child Benefit stops if a child starts an apprenticeship **in England**, but they don't explicitly address what happens with apprenticeships in Northern Ireland, Scotland, or Wales.

**What you should do:**

I recommend you **contact the Child Benefit Office directly** to clarify how Alex's apprenticeship in Northern Ireland affects your entitlement. They will be able to give you a definitive answer based on the complete rules for all UK nations.

You can contact them:
- By phone or post (check the gov.uk website for contact details)
- Through the online form on the HMRC website

They'll be able to confirm whether you can continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex while he's doing his apprenticeship in Belfast.
